passages.text: In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. And a certain man from Bethlehem in Judah, with his wife and two sons, went to reside in the land of Moab.
passages.sermon:
The judges ruled Israel during this time.
A famine came to the land.
A man lived in Bethlehem in Judah.
He had a wife.
He had two sons.
This man left Bethlehem.
He went to live in the fields of Moab.
His wife and his two sons went with him.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בִּימֵי֙ שְׁפֹ֣ט הַשֹּׁפְטִ֔ים וַיְהִ֥י רָעָ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אִ֜ישׁ מִבֵּ֧ית לֶ֣חֶם יְהוּדָ֗ה לָגוּר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב ה֥וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah, and they entered the land of Moab and settled there.
passages.sermon:
The man’s name was Elimelech.
His wife’s name was Naomi.
His two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion.
They were Ephrathites.
They came from Bethlehem in Judah.
They entered the land of Moab.
They settled there.
passages.original: וְשֵׁ֣ם הָאִ֣ישׁ אֱ‍ֽלִימֶ֡לֶךְ וְשֵׁם֩ אִשְׁתּ֨וֹ נָעֳמִ֜י וְשֵׁ֥ם שְׁנֵֽי־ בָנָ֣יו׀ מַחְל֤וֹן וְכִלְיוֹן֙ אֶפְרָתִ֔ים מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ שְׂדֵי־ מוֹאָ֖ב וַיִּֽהְיוּ־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Then Naomi’s husband Elimelech died, and she was left with her two sons, who took Moabite women as their wives, one named Orpah and the other named Ruth. And after they had lived in Moab about ten years, both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband.
passages.sermon:
Elimelech was Naomi’s husband.
Elimelech died.
Naomi remained alive.
Naomi had two sons.
Naomi’s two sons took wives from Moab.
One wife was named Orpah.
The other wife was named Ruth.
Naomi, her two sons, Orpah, and Ruth lived in Moab for about ten years.
Mahlon and Chilion were Naomi’s two sons.
Mahlon and Chilion both died.
Naomi was left without her two sons.
Naomi was left without her husband.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִימֶ֖לֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ נָעֳמִ֑י וַתִּשָּׁאֵ֥ר הִ֖יא וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנֶֽיהָ׃ וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם נָשִׁים֙ מֹֽאֲבִיּ֔וֹת שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָרְפָּ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית ר֑וּת וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ שָׁ֖ם כְּעֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃ וַיָּמ֥וּתוּ גַם־ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם מַחְל֣וֹן וְכִלְי֑וֹן וַתִּשָּׁאֵר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה מִשְּׁנֵ֥י יְלָדֶ֖יהָ וּמֵאִישָֽׁהּ׃

passages.text: When Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food, she and her daughters-in-law prepared to leave the land of Moab.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was a widow from Bethlehem in Judah.
She lived in the land of Moab with her two daughters-in-law.
Naomi heard news while she was in Moab.
She heard that the LORD had helped His people.
The LORD had given food to His people in Judah.
Naomi decided to leave the land of Moab.
Her two daughters-in-law prepared to leave with her.
passages.original: וַתָּ֤קָם הִיא֙ וְכַלֹּתֶ֔יהָ וַתָּ֖שָׁב מִשְּׂדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֑ב כִּ֤י שָֽׁמְעָה֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב כִּֽי־ פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ עַמּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: Accompanied by her two daughters-in-law, she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road leading back to the land of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was a widow from Moab.
She had lost her husband Elimelech and her two sons Mahlon and Chilion.
She had two daughters-in-law.
Their names were Orpah and Ruth.
Naomi decided to leave the place where she had been living.
Her two daughters-in-law went with her.
They all set out together.
They walked on the road.
They planned to return to the land of Judah.
passages.original: וַתֵּצֵ֗א מִן־ הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיְתָה־ שָׁ֔מָּה וּשְׁתֵּ֥י כַלֹּתֶ֖יהָ עִמָּ֑הּ וַתֵּלַ֣כְנָה בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ לָשׁ֖וּב אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s home. May the LORD show you loving devotion, as you have shown to your dead and to me.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was a widow from Bethlehem.
She lived in Moab with her two daughters-in-law.
Naomi spoke to her two daughters-in-law.
She said, “Go back.
Each of you should return to your mother’s home.
May the LORD show kindness to you.
You showed kindness to your husbands who have died.
You also showed kindness to me.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר נָעֳמִי֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י כַלֹּתֶ֔יהָ לֵ֣כְנָה שֹּׁ֔בְנָה אִשָּׁ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית אִמָּ֑הּ יַעֲשֶׂה יְהוָ֤ה עִמָּכֶם֙ חֶ֔סֶד כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֛ם עִם־ הַמֵּתִ֖ים וְעִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.” And she kissed them as they wept aloud and said, “Surely we will return with you to your people.”
passages.sermon:
Naomi was the mother-in-law of Ruth and Orpah.
Naomi spoke to Ruth and Orpah.
Naomi said, “May the LORD give you rest.
May each of you find rest in the home of a new husband.”
Naomi kissed Ruth and Orpah.
Ruth and Orpah raised their voices.
They wept aloud.
Ruth and Orpah said to Naomi, “We will return with you to your people.”
passages.original: יִתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ לָכֶ֔ם וּמְצֶ֣אןָ מְנוּחָ֔ה אִשָּׁ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אִישָׁ֑הּ וַתִּשַּׁ֣ק לָהֶ֔ן וַתִּשֶּׂ֥אנָה קוֹלָ֖ן וַתִּבְכֶּֽינָה׃ וַתֹּאמַ֖רְנָה־ לָּ֑הּ כִּי־ אִתָּ֥ךְ נָשׁ֖וּב לְעַמֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: But Naomi replied, “Return home, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb to become your husbands?
passages.sermon:
Naomi spoke to her daughters-in-law.
Naomi said, "Return home, my daughters."
Naomi asked, "Why would you go with me?"
Naomi said, "I do not have more sons in my womb."
Naomi said, "These sons cannot become your husbands."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר נָעֳמִי֙ שֹׁ֣בְנָה בְנֹתַ֔י לָ֥מָּה תֵלַ֖כְנָה עִמִּ֑י הַֽעֽוֹד־ לִ֤י בָנִים֙ בְּֽמֵעַ֔י וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם לַאֲנָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Return home, my daughters. Go on, for I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was hope for me to have a husband tonight and to bear sons, would you wait for them to grow up? Would you refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, it grieves me very much for your sakes that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.”
passages.sermon:
Naomi spoke to her daughters-in-law.
Naomi told them to return home.
Naomi said, "Go on, my daughters."
Naomi explained that she was too old to have another husband.
Naomi said, "Even if I thought there was hope for me."
Naomi said, "Even if I could have a husband tonight."
Naomi said, "Even if I could bear sons."
Naomi asked, "Would you wait for them to grow up?"
Naomi asked, "Would you remain unmarried for them?"
Naomi said, "No, my daughters."
Naomi said, "It grieves me very much for your sakes."
Naomi said, "The hand of the LORD has gone out against me."
passages.original: שֹׁ֤בְנָה בְנֹתַי֙ לֵ֔כְןָ כִּ֥י זָקַ֖נְתִּי מִהְי֣וֹת לְאִ֑ישׁ כִּ֤י אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ יֶשׁ־ לִ֣י תִקְוָ֔ה גַּ֣ם הָיִ֤יתִי הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ לְאִ֔ישׁ וְגַ֖ם יָלַ֥דְתִּי בָנִֽים׃ הֲלָהֵ֣ן׀ תְּשַׂבֵּ֗רְנָה עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגְדָּ֔לוּ הֲלָהֵן֙ תֵּֽעָגֵ֔נָה לְבִלְתִּ֖י הֱי֣וֹת לְאִ֑ישׁ אַ֣ל בְּנֹתַ֗י כִּֽי־ מַר־ לִ֤י מְאֹד֙ מִכֶּ֔ם כִּֽי־ יָצְאָ֥ה בִ֖י יַד־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Again they wept aloud, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was the mother-in-law of Orpah and Ruth.
Orpah and Ruth were both widows.
Orpah and Ruth raised their voices and wept again.
Orpah kissed her mother-in-law Naomi goodbye.
Ruth did not leave Naomi.
Ruth clung to Naomi.
passages.original: וַתִּשֶּׂ֣נָה קוֹלָ֔ן וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ינָה ע֑וֹד וַתִּשַּׁ֤ק עָרְפָּה֙ לַחֲמוֹתָ֔הּ וְר֖וּת דָּ֥בְקָה בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: “Look,” said Naomi, “your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.”
passages.sermon:
Naomi spoke to Ruth.
Naomi said, "Look at your sister-in-law."
Your sister-in-law has returned to her own people.
She has gone back to her own gods.
Go back with your sister-in-law.
Follow her home.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה֙ שָׁ֣בָה יְבִמְתֵּ֔ךְ אֶל־ עַמָּ֖הּ וְאֶל־ אֱלֹהֶ֑יהָ שׁ֖וּבִי אַחֲרֵ֥י יְבִמְתֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: But Ruth replied: “Do not urge me to leave you or to turn from following you. For wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you live, I will live; your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
passages.sermon:
Ruth was a Moabite woman.
Ruth spoke to Naomi, her mother-in-law.
Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you.
Do not tell me to stop following you.
Where you go, I will go.
Where you stay, I will stay.
Your people will be my people.
Your God will be my God.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רוּת֙ אַל־ תִּפְגְּעִי־ בִ֔י לְעָזְבֵ֖ךְ לָשׁ֣וּב מֵאַחֲרָ֑יִךְ כִּ֠י אֶל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֵּלְכִ֜י אֵלֵ֗ךְ וּבַאֲשֶׁ֤ר תָּלִ֙ינִי֙ אָלִ֔ין עַמֵּ֣ךְ עַמִּ֔י וֵאלֹהַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.”
passages.sermon:
Ruth was a Moabite woman.
Ruth spoke to Naomi, her Israelite mother-in-law.
Ruth said, “Where you die, I will die.
I will be buried there with you.
May the LORD punish me if I break this promise.
May the LORD punish me even more if anything but death separates us.”
passages.original: בַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר תָּמ֙וּתִי֙ אָמ֔וּת וְשָׁ֖ם אֶקָּבֵ֑ר כֹּה֩ יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י הַמָּ֔וֶת יַפְרִ֖יד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was Ruth’s mother-in-law.
Ruth was a Moabite woman.
Ruth wanted to go with Naomi to Bethlehem.
Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her.
Naomi stopped speaking to Ruth about turning back.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֕רֶא כִּֽי־ מִתְאַמֶּ֥צֶת הִ֖יא לָלֶ֣כֶת אִתָּ֑הּ וַתֶּחְדַּ֖ל לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: So Naomi and Ruth traveled until they came to Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the whole city was stirred because of them, and the women of the city exclaimed, “Can this be Naomi?”
passages.sermon:
Naomi was an Israelite woman.
Ruth was her daughter-in-law from Moab.
Naomi and Ruth traveled together.
They walked until they reached Bethlehem.
They entered the city of Bethlehem.
The people in the city noticed them.
The whole city became excited because of Naomi and Ruth.
The women of Bethlehem saw Naomi.
The women asked, “Is this Naomi?”
passages.original: וַתֵּלַ֣כְנָה שְׁתֵּיהֶ֔ם עַד־ בֹּאָ֖נָה בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם וַיְהִ֗י כְּבֹאָ֙נָה֙ בֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם וַתֵּהֹ֤ם כָּל־ הָעִיר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ן וַתֹּאמַ֖רְנָה הֲזֹ֥את נָעֳמִֽי׃

passages.text: “Do not call me Naomi,” she replied. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was a woman from Bethlehem.
She had returned from Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth.
The women of Bethlehem saw Naomi and spoke to her.
Naomi said to them, “Do not call me Naomi.”
She said, “Call me Mara.”
She said, “The Almighty has made my life very bitter.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ן אַל־ תִּקְרֶ֥אנָה לִ֖י נָעֳמִ֑י קְרֶ֤אןָ לִי֙ מָרָ֔א כִּי־ הֵמַ֥ר שַׁדַּ֛י לִ֖י מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? After all, the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me.”
passages.sermon:
Naomi was a woman from Bethlehem.
She left her home with much.
She says, "I went away full."
The LORD brought her back with nothing.
She says, "The LORD has brought me back empty."
She asks, "Why do you call me Naomi?"
She says, "The LORD has testified against me."
She says, "The Almighty has brought trouble to me."
passages.original: אֲנִי֙ מְלֵאָ֣ה הָלַ֔כְתִּי וְרֵיקָ֖ם הֱשִׁיבַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה לָ֣מָּה תִקְרֶ֤אנָה לִי֙ נָעֳמִ֔י וַֽיהוָה֙ עָ֣נָה בִ֔י וְשַׁדַּ֖י הֵ֥רַֽע לִֽי׃

passages.text: So Naomi returned from the land of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabitess. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
passages.sermon:
Naomi was a widow from Bethlehem.
Ruth was Naomi’s daughter-in-law.
Ruth was a Moabite woman.
Naomi and Ruth returned together from the land of Moab.
They both came to Bethlehem.
They arrived at the beginning of the barley harvest.
passages.original: וַתָּ֣שָׁב נָעֳמִ֗י וְר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֤ה כַלָּתָהּ֙ עִמָּ֔הּ הַשָּׁ֖בָה מִשְּׂדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֑ב וְהֵ֗מָּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת קְצִ֥יר שְׂעֹרִֽים׃
